title: Seller identity block
question: Does the store say who sells: a legal name, a geographic address and an email address?
method: Read the imprint (legal-notice) page and the contact page found in the home page links, the home page itself, and their Organization JSON-LD. A legal name is a company form in the text (GmbH, Ltd, Inc., S.A. and the like) or an Organization legalName or name. A postal address is a street with a house number or a postcode next to a place name in the text, or a PostalAddress with a streetAddress in the markup. An email address is one in the text, a mailto: link or an email in the Organization markup. Found when all three are present, review when one or two are, not found when none is. A contact form alone is not an email address. Whether the details are true cannot be checked.

spec.title: UK Electronic Commerce (EC Directive) Regulations 2002, regulation 6

title: Registration and tax numbers
question: Does the store show the registration or tax numbers its markets ask for?
method: Read the imprint, contact, terms and home pages and look for the identifier each detected market asks for. EU: a VAT ID, usually after a label such as VAT, USt-IdNr. or TVA, format checked per country. UK: a company number after wording such as "company number" or "registered in England", format checked. Switzerland: a UID (CHE, mod 11 check digit). Brazil: a CNPJ (two check digits). Chile: a RUT (mod 11). Colombia: a NIT (DIAN check digit). Argentina: a CUIT (mod 11). Peru: a RUC (mod 11). Found when every detected market has a valid number. Review when a number fails its check digit or only some markets are covered. Not found when no number is present. The UK registered office and the part of the UK where the company is registered are not checked.

spec.title: UK Company, LLP and Business (Names and Trading Disclosures) Regulations 2015

title: Libro de Reclamaciones (Peru)
question: Does the store link its virtual complaints book?
method: Found when the home page has a link, button or image whose text, aria-label, title or alt text contains "Libro de Reclamaciones". Not found otherwise. Runs only when the store appears to sell to Peru.

spec.title: Peru Código de Protección y Defensa del Consumidor (Ley 29571), Articles 150 and 151

title: No outdated dispute-resolution link
question: Does the store still point consumers to the EU ODR platform, which closed in July 2025?
method: Read the home page, the terms and the imprint. Review when they link to ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr or name the ODR (online dispute resolution) platform, for example "OS-Plattform" or "online dispute resolution platform". Found (nothing outdated) otherwise. The ODR Regulation was repealed with effect from 20 July 2025, so the link leads nowhere. This is a tidy-up of legal text, not a breach.
